summary: Abigail sends two hundred fig cakes to David. Later his men give a starving traveler a piece of one. The same preparation is laid on Hezekiah’s boil.

senses.definition: Figs pressed together in a mass that can be carried whole or divided into portions.

evidence.note: Abigail loads two hundred cakes on donkeys with bread, wine and other provisions.
David’s men give the Egyptian a piece of one cake along with raisins.
Fig cakes and raisins are among the foods brought to David at Hebron.
At Isaiah’s direction a cake of figs is laid on Hezekiah’s sore.
Isaiah’s parallel instruction names figs as the material to be spread on the boil.

evidence.locator: p. 82, ܕܒܠܬܐ, alone or with the word for figs

cognates.gloss: compact lump, portion of kneaded food

evidence.locator: p. 850, n12069, compare the food shaped by hand in n12065

note: Egyptian Aramaic also attests דבלה for a fig cake (TAD D1.11:2, indexed by Muraoka and Porten in A Grammar of Egyptian Aramaic). The place Diblah occurs in Ezk.6.14. The verse gives no explanation of its name.
